title: Atlas Securities — AML assistant prototype notes
content:
Meeting: 2026-02-19 call w/ Atlas Securities (initial scoping)
Attendees (Atlas): Adam R. (Head of Ops), Lina K. (AML investigator), Tomas V. (Platform eng)
Attendees (Redwood): Maya Chen (solutions), Ethan Rios (infra), Priya M. (security)

Quick summary:
- Atlas wants an assistant to triage and augment AML alerts (reduce investigator time + false positives).
- Hard requirement: No customer PII or account numbers leave Atlas environment. So Hosted API is off the table unless they accept strong tokenization (they do not). Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) likely.
- Primary flows: alert enrichment (contextual history, entity linking), risk-scoring reranker, suggestion of next steps (watchlist checks, escalate), and auto-population of case fields in their internal CRM.

Goals / success metrics (customer stated):
- 30% reduction in time-per-case for Tier-1 alerts (target 2.5 min -> 1.75 min)
- 20% drop in FP P1s flagged by current rules in 90d pilot
- Precision >= 0.65 at recall >= 0.8 for high-risk class (initial threshold for evaluation)

Constraints / non-functional:
- Data residency: private VPC inside AWS eu-west-2 (London) preferred; legal team may push for fully on-prem later.
- Audit: all LLM inputs/outputs must be logged with immutable IDs; retention policy configurable per customer (90d default).
- Latency SLO: investigator UX: when pressing "Enrich" must get first partial response within 1.5s and final within 6s for typical 512-token context. This is aggressive — may need smaller contexts or local KV cache.
- Throughput: expect 10 concurrent investigators during business peaks -> plan for burst capacity on Dedicated pools if Private can't autoscale horizontally.
- Key mgmt: integrate with customer KMS/HSM.

Data & model considerations:
- Training/eval data: Atlas will provide 2k labeled alerts + redacted audit logs for initial eval. We should request a 1:5 mixture of true positive:false positive to mimic ops distribution (they currently have high FP rate).
- For initial prototype: recommend a reranker + embedding-based similarity for enrichment; do not fine-tune until eval shows gains. Use quantized 8-bit model on Private GPU pool.
- Consider small local classifier (logistic/LightGBM) on top of LLM embeddings for speed-critical decisions. LLM used for explainability + suggestions.

Integration notes (dev ops):
- Hooks: webhook -> Redwood private endpoint -> enrich -> return JSON payload w/fields: risk_score, suggested_tags, summary, source_snippets (token offsets), confidence
- Need strong schema and versioning for the payload; Atlas insisted on stable schema v1 for at least 3 months.
- Case CRM mapping: we will send mapping doc for fields; Tomas to share their CRM API docs (action: Tomas 2026-02-23).

Security & compliance gotchas:
- PII redaction: their redaction rules are complicated (account numbers sometimes partial). We should not rely solely on model redaction; recommend pre-masking at integration layer.
- Adversarial inputs: AML actors sometimes insert noise to evade detection. Add adversarial examples to eval set.
- Legal: they asked for paper trail showing how decisions are made — include the model prompt, deterministic tokenizer snapshot, and reranker weights (or model hash).

UX / product thoughts (notes):
- Investigator "Enrich" button should show succinct summary + up to 3 recommended next actions (e.g., escalate, close as false pos, attach to existing case).
- Provide an "explain" panel that surfaces top-3 supporting snippets (timestamped) and similar historical cases with links.
- Option to "flag model suggestion" to collect correction data (we want that for online eval loop).

Initial spike plan (deliverables + timeline):
1) Tech spike: deploy Redwood Private instance in Atlas test VPC with sample sanitized logs; integrate webhook prototype; produce first-pass enrichment responses (10 business days) -> owner: Ethan (due 2026-03-03)
2) Eval harness: ingest Atlas provided 2k labeled alerts, run baseline (current rules) vs LLM reranker + embedding similarity, produce PR/metrics dashboard (precision/recall, time-to-first-byte) (14 days) -> owner: Priya (due 2026-03-10)
3) Security review & KMS integration proof-of-concept (KMS token rotation + audit logs) (7 days) -> owner: Maya (due 2026-03-06)
4) Business demo + SOW draft (10 days after eval) -> owner: Maya + Solutions Eng (target demo 2026-03-18)

Action items (shorthand):
- Tomas (Atlas): share CRM API + sample sanitized event log (due 2026-02-23)
- Atlas legal: confirm retention window + whether logs may leave VPC (asked 2026-02-19)
- Ethan: spin up test Private stack (eu-west-2), pre-load lightweight model, test latency baseline (due 2026-03-03)
- Priya: build eval harness, create Jupyter notebook + dashboard, include adversarial test cases (due 2026-03-10)
- Maya: draft SOW + cost estimate for 3-month pilot (due 2026-03-12)

Risks & open questions:
- If Atlas insists on fully air-gapped on-prem, cost/time increases significantly — need to precompute delta and present options.
- Latency SLO may be unrealistic for full 2048-token contexts; propose progressive reveal + caching.
- Data labeling: their in-house labels are noisy; we may need label-cleaning steps. Budget that in.

Prompt sketches (rough — for internal use):
- System: "You are an AML analyst assistant. Given the alert record and recent activity, provide a concise risk summary (1-2 sentences), a numerical risk score 0-1, and up to 3 recommended next steps with rationale. Return structured JSON."
- User example: input = {alert_id, account_history_snippets, watchlist_matches, transaction_examples} -> output = {score, summary, actions:[{label, reason}], supporting_snippets:[{text, ts}] }

Notes to self (misc):
- Emphasize immutable logging requirement in SOW (auditability is a blocker).
- For demo, prepare 6 curated cases: 2 true money-laundering, 2 false positives, 2 borderline that benefit from context.
- Cost options: show Hosted (low friction) vs Dedicated (predictable) vs Private (compliant). They will push Private.

Next sync: 2026-02-26 10:00am PT (internal prep 9:30am PT)

Random shorthand / brainstorming:
- Could we offer an on-device tokenizer + prefix cache to reduce roundtrips? (Ethan thinks feasible)
- Explore lightweight rules layer to catch deterministic PII pre-send.

---- end notes ----
